message.content: Compared to prior CXRs: edema and possible pneumonia resolved; heart top-normal, improved; pleural effusions resolved. Right hilar vessel enlargement (possible PAH). LCx atherosclerotic calcification.
Heart/mediastinum stable. Bilateral multifocal mid/lower-lobe opacities (peripheral/basal). No effusion, pneumothorax, or edema. DDx: infection, COP, drug reaction. Recommend chest CT.
Decreased bilateral pleural effusions, now small. Mild left lower lobe atelectasis unchanged. No pneumothorax. Neoesophagus remains large and fluid-filled.
Right lower mediastinal contour enlarged; likely dilated gastric pull-up with associated atelectasis. Findings have fluctuated on prior films. Consider pull-up obstruction if recent vomiting.
Cardiac size stable. Basal interstitial markings: vascular congestion vs ILD; CT needed for ILD dx. Bibasilar atelectasis; possible pleural fluid/thickening. RV apical lead. No acute focal PNA.
Normal heart size and mediastinum. Lungs well inflated. No pleural effusion, pneumothorax, consolidation, or mediastinal/hilar adenopathy (within study limits). Consider chest CT if indicated.
New left pectoral pacemaker with leads to RA and RV; lead course unremarkable. No pneumothorax, pleural effusions, or pulmonary edema. Left basal atelectasis unchanged.
Two L chest tubes (apical and to L CPA). Stable apical loculated air—postop change vs PTX; f/u advised. Small L SQ emphysema. No consolidation/effusion. Stable R pleural thickening (likely talc).
Right apical pneumothorax unchanged; no tension. s/p right upper lobe wedge resection. Moderate cardiomegaly unchanged. Minimal left basilar atelectasis. No large pleural effusions.
Slightly lower lung volumes vs prior. Extensive bilateral coarse interstitial changes, greater in L mid/lower zones; consistent with chronic ILD (NSIP). Cannot exclude superimposed acute pneumonia.
Longstanding moderate cardiomegaly. Mediastinal venous engorgement slightly increased vs prior. No pulm vascular engorgement/edema. Mild R base atelectasis likely. Left effusion minimal, if any.
No acute intrathoracic process. Apical pleural thickening R>L, likely scarring. Recommend prior comparison; if unavailable, repeat chest X-ray in 3 months. Findings discussed by phone.
No acute intrathoracic process. Right-greater apical pleural thickening, likely scarring. Recommend comparison with priors or 3-month follow-up CXR. Findings discussed with clinician by phone.
Similar to prior. No acute cardiopulmonary disease: normal heart size; no vascular congestion, pleural effusion, or focal pneumonia. Mild mid-thoracic vertebral body height loss, unchanged.
Left pleural catheter stable; tip inf/post. No pneumothorax. Stable left basilar opacity likely atelectasis + small-moderate pleural effusion. Emphysema stable. Right lung clear. Heart obscured.
Moderate L, small R pleural effusions, slightly increased. Stable mild postop cardiomegaly. Tiny unchanged L apical pneumothorax. Improved moderately severe LLL atelectasis. No pulmonary edema.
Hyperinflated lungs. Right apical bulla with asymmetric right apicolateral pleural thickening. Lung CA risk: chest CT to exclude apical mass. Right infrahilar asymmetry (vessels vs mass) for CT.
Vs prior CXR: Postop left hemithorax unchanged: volume loss with leftward mediastinal shift, atelectasis, and left basilar effusion. Right lung clear; possible new 15 mm RLL nodule c/w outside CT.
Apical pneumothorax slightly increased (still small-mod), likely from chest tube removal/reposition. R base unchanged; possible slight inc right pleural effusion; small left effusion not excluded.
Unchanged cardiomegaly & tortuous aorta/mediastinum. Stable interstitial/subpleural opacities; bronchiectasis. Increased right apical consolidation. No new consolidation; no effusion or pneumothorax.
Suspected mild RUL and bibasilar atelectasis. Probable right upper lung granulomas. No PTX, pneumomediastinum, esoph. air-fluid level, or radiopaque FB. Top sternal wire fx. No other acute process.

CXR: Bilateral hilar enlargement (L>R) and med. lobulation c/w central adenopathy. Possible granulomatous calcs vs vessels. No suspicious nodules. Heart normal; no effusion. DDx: sarcoid, lymphoma/met.
Persistent left apical pneumothorax with endobronchial valves over left hilum in severe emphysema. Mild left basilar atelectasis. Right lung clear. No vascular congestion.
Right chest trauma; prior exam lacked these changes. New acute infiltrates: LUL lingula and RLL posterior segment. Follow-up chest imaging after treatment; query prior severe thoracic trauma.
No radiopaque esophageal foreign body. Slightly increased right lung apex scarring; concern for reactivation TB—correlate clinically (cough). Emailed ED nurses 8:05 a.m. after attending review.
Lobulated dense right hilar contour suspicious for lymphadenopathy. Recommend contrast-enhanced chest CT. No prior films for comparison. No evidence of pneumonia.
Large right hydropneumothorax with increased air/fluid, no mediastinal shift. Subcutaneous emphysema improved but persists. Left basilar atelectasis improved.
Stable. R pleural thickening with loculated mod effusion; R base opac from RLL lesion + atelectasis; R basal interstitial changes c/w lymphangitic spread; B/L pulmonary nodules better seen prior.
CXR: Large R pleural effusion obscuring most of R lung. No mediastinal shift; likely fixed by tumor along trachea displacing R bronchi inferiorly. L lung clear. Nurse notified.
New multifocal alveolar/interstitial opacities with small bilateral effusions. DDx: atypical edema, opportunistic infection, PTLD. ESRD noted. Recheck post-dialysis; if no improvement, chest CT.
New multifocal alveolar/interstitial opacities with small bilateral effusions. DDx: atypical edema, opportunistic infection, PTLD. ESRD: repeat CXR after dialysis; if unchanged, get chest CT.
Left lung nodule not nipple; less distinct, possibly resolving inflam. Repeat PA/lateral/oblq CXR in 2 wks; CT same day if persists. Heart top-normal; lungs clear; no pleural dz; RA/RV pacer leads OK
Right pleural effusion unchanged. Slightly more nodular mid/upper pleural thickening (may be positional). Postsurgical right upper lung sutures; prior PET favored recurrence. Left lung clear.
Small right pneumothorax slightly increased; subcutaneous emphysema improved; small-moderate right effusion slightly larger; left effusion stable; postop CM enlargement unchanged.
Left chest tube in place; small left apical pneumothorax; possible intrafissural. Persistent LLL atelectasis; minimal right basilar atelectasis. Small bilateral effusions. Known left rib fractures.
Stable layering right pleural effusion with airspace disease (atelectasis vs pneumonia). Cardiomegaly vs pericardial effusion. Aortic calcification (atherosclerosis). No PTX/left effusion.
Better inspiration vs prior. Bilateral alveolar/interstitial opacities suggest asymmetric edema. Left improved; possible superimposed right-lung pneumonia. No substantial pleural effusion.
Compared to prior, lung volumes are lower, likely making heart appear larger. Retrocardiac opacity favors atelectasis; pneumonia not excluded. No vascular congestion. Central line to mid-lower SVC.
Minimal L costophrenic blunting and L base opacity; c/w atelectasis/scar with small effusion or chronic pleural thickening; early infection possible. No edema/pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinum normal.
Likely pneumonia in superior segment of LLL; prior left basilar opacity resolved. Possible tiny left pleural effusion. Right lung clear. Cardiomediastinal contours stable. No edema or pneumothorax.
Right chest tube in place. Moderate likely loculated effusion persists with mediastinal shift and marked right atelectasis. Left lung clear; tiny left effusion. Heart not enlarged; vessels normal.
Median sternotomy with AVR/MVR. Right subclavian stent unchanged. Improved moderate cardiomegaly. No pulmonary edema or pneumonia. Left base elevation likely from pleural scarring.
Cardiomegaly and mediastinal vessels enlarged; right pleural effusion larger. New bibasilar opacities, atelectasis vs pneumonia, not asymmetric edema. Chronic posterior base elevation, likely left.
Normal heart; effusions resolved. RUL pneumonia/LLL atelectasis improved; residual basal & lingular atelectasis. No active pneumonia/CHF. s/p CABG. Severe COPD hyperinflation. No amiodarone toxicity.
Cardiomegaly without vascular congestion, suggesting cardiomyopathy. Left subclavian dual-channel pacer with RA and RV apical leads. No pneumothorax. Small bilateral pleural effusions.
Right PIC line at cavoatrial junction. Moderate right pleural effusion, stable. Moderately severe RLL atelectasis. RUL and left lung clear. Heart size normal. Small left effusion; chronicity unclear.
Compared to prior CXR, resolved mild pulmonary edema; no pneumonia. Severe cardiomegaly persists. Right paratracheal fullness likely distended azygos vein per prior CTA. No pleural abnormality.
No interval or acute change: healing rib fractures; elevated right hemidiaphragm; borderline cardiac size w/o pulm edema; min peribronchial interstitial thickening c/w chronic airways disease.
New mild cardiomegaly vs small pericardial effusion; new small right pleural effusion. No focal lung abnormality. Possible mild CHF. If not improving, repeat CXR; low threshold for chest CT.
Unchanged: large R lung nodule, bilateral apical opacities, and para-aortic LN calcifications. If symptoms persist, pneumonia still suspected. 4–5 mm opacity at ventral L 4th rib better seen.

Right chest tubes removed. No significant pneumothorax; possible loculated air at right base/apex. Stable right base opacity (postsurgical/atelectasis) s/p VATS pleurodesis/diaphragm repair. No edema.
Stable CXR: no pneumonia, edema, or effusions. Low lung volumes; cardiac size normal. Right PICC unchanged with tip at cavoatrial junction. Hepatic embolization material unchanged.
Bilateral hilar prominence, possibly vascular or symmetric lymphadenopathy (e.g., sarcoidosis). Compare to prior CXRs; if none, consider contrast chest CT to assess hila.
Stable heart and mediastinum. Elevated left hemidiaphragm of uncertain chronicity with linear left basilar atelectasis; upper lungs clear. Chest CT recommended for further characterization.
Low lung volumes limiting assessment. No pneumothorax. Bibasilar atelectasis (R>L); infection not excluded. Repeat inspiratory CXR if indicated. No acute chest wall injury; CT/bone films for trauma.

Bibasilar opacities likely atelectasis; mildly elevated R hemidiaphragm; inf/asp not excluded. Central pulm vascularity suggests mild edema; low volumes may accentuate. Poss. trace R pleural effusion.
Postop mediastinum normal; heart upper-normal. Small effusions: R stable, L decreased. LLL atelectasis improved. No edema. Bilateral opacities—pleural calcifications vs lesions; CT advised.

Left chest pacer leads in expected position. No pneumothorax/effusion/mediastinal widening; heart size normal, no edema. Post-CABG sternotomy. RUL peribronchial change: scar vs acute pneumonia—correlate clinically.
Unchanged chest: hyperinflated lungs/flattened diaphragms c/w COPD; mild mid-thoracic compression; stable left lateral pleural thickening; no pneumonia, vascular congestion, or effusion.
Normal lung volumes. Borderline enlarged cardiac silhouette; no edema. No pneumonia, nodules, or masses. If symptoms persist, consider chest CT for subtle changes.
Left chest tube and other devices removed. Possible small L apical pneumothorax. R effusion with fissural fluid; mild R basilar atelectasis. No L pneumonia. Postop mediast/pericardial air resolved.
R pleural effusion down; L same/slightly up. Pulm edema unchanged. Heart top-normal. R hilar vascular enlargement suggests biventricular failure. No mediastinal nodes. Port tip upper RA unchanged.
Stable moderate left pleural effusion; prior right effusion resolved. Severe cardiomegaly stable; lungs clear. RA pacer lead more horizontal on frontal, lateral unchanged. RV ICD lead unchanged.
Since prior, near-complete clearing of left base opacity. Residual likely atelectasis/effusion; posterior LLL pneumonia cannot be excluded. Otherwise normal; no vascular congestion.
Small mid-thoracic atelectasis on lateral. Lungs otherwise clear post bilateral resections. No effusion or central adenopathy. Chronic elevated right base. Heart normal size, partly obscured postop.

Mid/lower lung patchy interstitial opacities → multifocal pneumonia, possible aspiration; follow-up advised. Known RUL spiculated mass not well seen. COPD. Findings phoned to Dr ___ at 1:01 pm on ___.
Cardiomediastinal contours normal. No PTX, pneumomediastinum, effusions, or consolidation. Lungs clear; no acute bony injury. LLL nodular opacities likely vessels-on-end; no LUL nodule. F/u chest CT.
Large RLL mass with right hilar/subcarinal LAD; c/w NSCLC hx, likely lymphangitic spread and small R pleural effusion. New perimass opacities vs prior CT, c/w postobstructive pneumonia or hemorrhage.
Chronic low lung volumes; LLL atelectasis; increased vasc./interstitial chg/cuffing vs prior; borderline cardiomegaly; ILD vs CHF indet.; no effusion; T-L gibbus; mod-sev compression fxs unchanged.
Vs prior: Left basolateral consolidation decreased, now diffuse opacity. Left costophrenic blunting persists; pleural extent clearer on lateral. No new opacities. Heart size stable; no pneumothorax.
Hyperinflated lungs without focal consolidation; diffuse interstitial markings may be chronic change vs edema. Severe lower thoracic compression deformity, age indeterminate; correlate clinically.
Vs prior CXR: mod right pleural effusion with right basilar atelectasis (seen on outside PET-CT, date unk). Mod cardiomegaly w/o edema. LUL nodule. Vertebral compression fx unchanged (lateral only).
Left chest tube removed; residual SQ emphysema. Bilateral opacities/distortion c/w bullous emphysema. Left loculated PTX and hydropneumothorax; no interval change. Cardiomediastinum likely stable.
R apical pneumothorax unchanged. Increased R lower chest air/fluid loculations; pleural vs lung source unclear—CT advised incl catheter position. L lung hyperinflated/clear; heart upper normal size.
Unchanged small R apical pneumothorax. Increased R lower chest air-fluid loculations, likely pleural vs lung despite R drain; CT to confirm/localize catheter. L lung hyperinflated; heart top-normal.
Left hilar rounded mass enlarged vs prior; CT recommended for localization. Left apical reticular opacities stable. Borderline cardiac silhouette. No pleural effusions.
Left hilar mass-like lesion enlarged vs prior; CT recommended for localization. Left apical reticular opacities stable. Borderline cardiac silhouette size. No pleural effusions.

Post-CABG median sternotomy; stable cardiomediastinal contours. Lungs inflated; no consolidation/PNA, pulm edema, pleural effusions, or PTX. Old R posterior rib deformity and old R midclavicle fracture.
Chronic stable pleural thickening/scarring at right costophrenic angle. Stable calcified right lower lobe nodule, may represent calcified granuloma. No pneumonia.

New lobulated pleural-based opacity in right lower hemithorax; loculated effusion vs hemothorax. Chest CT recommended. Bilateral effusions and multiple bilateral lung nodules c/w metastases unchanged.
Left pectoral Port-a-Cath tip now malpositioned in azygos vein. 3–4 mm calcified subpleural right apical granuloma. No pleural effusion, pneumonia, or pulmonary edema. Heart size normal.

RUL cavitary disease decreased; now no cavitation; RUL scarring persists. Left 2nd rib opacity possibly sclerotic (better on CT from ___). Prior CT cavities incl fungus ball not seen now. No effusion.
Heart/mediastinum stable. RUL opacity improved but persistent, suspicious for pneumonia. No effusion or pneumothorax. Repeat CXR 4 wks after antibiotics; consider chest CT if persistent/other dx.
Stable. Cardiomegaly without vascular congestion; ?cardiomyopathy. Dual-chamber pacer with RA/RV apical leads unchanged; no pneumothorax. Peripheral bilateral pleural plaques. No acute pneumonia.
New AV pacer leads in expected course. No PTX. Small left pleural eff. persists post drain removal. Elevated R hemidiaphragm may hide small R eff. RLL atelectasis. Heart size normal. L lung clear.
L lung clear. R hemidiaphragm markedly elevated, unchanged. RLL atelectasis; possible peribronchial opacities in RML and near L hilum (infection/aspiration). No edema or large effusion. Heart normal.
Vs prior CXR: stable LLL opacity and left effusion; new milder R base changes. Bilateral pattern favors aspiration over pneumonia. Moderate cardiomegaly, no overt pulmonary edema or pneumothorax.
No evidence of active TB or granulomatous infection. Bibasilar opacities—possible aspiration/bacterial pneumonia; CXR follow-up. Small bilateral pleural effusions. Cardiomegaly, no pulmonary edema.
Clear lungs with hyperinflation suggestive of COPD. Hemoptysis etiology indeterminate; consider chest CT. RLL nodular opacity likely nipple shadow; confirm with nipple views or CT.
Recurrent left upper lobe pneumonia in a chronically abnormal area; atypical mycobacterial infection considered. Results communicated at 11:30 p.m. and 8:03 a.m.

Normal lung volumes. Enlarged right hilum with mass; possible middle lobe atelectasis. Suspicious; CT advised. Moderate cardiomegaly, mild descending aortic elongation. No pneumonia, edema, effusions.
No focal consolidation/pneumonia. Nonspecific right hilar abnormal density, possible adenopathy. Recommend repeat PA chest X-ray or chest CT for evaluation.
Stable exam: bilateral pleural effusions unchanged, redistributed by positioning; best seen on lateral/frontal. No pneumonia, no new parenchymal changes, no pulmonary edema. Cardiac size stable.
No active cardiopulmonary disease. Possible right lung nodule, poorly localized—repeat CXR with PA + additional/shallow oblique views advised. Dilated ascending aorta; stability vs prior CTA unknown.
Moderate left pleural effusion enlarged post pigtail removal with pleural/left fissural loculations; lobulated mediastinum, adenopathy not excluded; no shift. Right midlung scar/atelectasis stable.
Better inflation. Prior basilar atelectasis cleared. Persistent pleural calcifications L>R. Minimal nonspecific left basilar scarring. No acute pneumonia or pulmonary edema.
New 3 cm crescentic LUL opacity, likely external; repeat frontal CXR with patient disrobed/hair out. Lungs otherwise clear; lateral: ↑ hyperinflation/flat diaph c/w small airways obstruction.
Lingular 3–3.8 cm opacity over cardiac apex; may reflect growth from prior lingular lesion vs acute pneumonia. Heart size normal; no effusion. New mod-severe lower thoracic vertebral height loss.
Chest X-ray: Mild hyperinflation suggesting emphysema. No pneumonia, effusion, or pulmonary edema. Heart normal size. Pleural thickening from healed fractures. Mediastinal/hilar contours normal.
Vs prior CXR: Swan-Ganz removed; no PTX. Stable cardiomegaly. Interstitial edema slightly decreased. Concern for RLL basilar pneumonia (retrocardiac opacity). Hyperinflated lungs c/w emphysema.
↑ small L pleural effusion and large L basal consolidation; apical chest tube in place. No pneumothorax. Concern for pneumonia. Cardiac silhouette slightly ↑. R base opacities ↑, likely atelectasis.
Small-mod L pleural effusion smaller after L pleural drain removal; no pneumothorax. L base aeration improved. Minimal R effusion and atelectasis stable. Mild cardiomegaly unchanged; no congestion.
Left PICC removed. Mild right-convex thoracic scoliosis. Normal cardiomediastinal silhouette. Persistent left basilar atelectasis. No pneumothoraces. Increased left pleural effusion (lateral view).
Compared to prior: Left PIC line in upper SVC. New left basilar subsegmental atelectasis. Tiny new left pleural effusion on lateral. No pneumonia; lungs otherwise clear; normal cardiohilar.
R IJ catheter at CAJ/upper RA. R supraclavicular lucency/opacity likely external. Improved lung volumes. Bibasilar opacities L>R c/w atelectasis + small effusion. No definite vascular congestion.
RIJ central line unchanged. Stable post-CABG chest. Bilat pleural effusions L>R. Left base opacity likely atelectasis; pneumonia unlikely. Vascular prominence, no edema. No pneumothorax.
L pigtail. L small eff ↑, min atelect, small–mod PTX. L rib fx. R small eff & min base atelect unchg. R base lucency likely artifact; exp view if PTX concern. R mid/lower nodule; CT f/u advised. COPD
Multifocal pneumonia, worst in RUL, with minimal improvement. New small right pleural effusion. Heart size upper normal; coronary stents. Right PICC tip in RA; withdraw 2 cm to low SVC.
Neo-esophagus dilated to 77 mm (was 16). Heart normal size, slightly larger. Lungs clear but hyperinflated; upper-lobe emphysema at least moderate–severe. No pneumothorax or effusion.
Left pectoral ICD: generator rotated vs prior (degree N/A); lead unchanged. Heart upper-normal/mildly enlarged; appears larger vs prior (position/cycle). No acute lung process. Correlate clinically.
Heart size normal; pulmonary vascularity now normal. Persistent left basal heterogeneous opacity: atelectasis vs pneumonia. Left costophrenic blunting again: effusion vs pleural thickening.
Compared to prior, heart size and pulmonary vascularity are normal. Persistent left basilar opacity—atelectasis vs pneumonia. Left costophrenic angle blunting: effusion vs pleural thickening.
Left base atelectasis likely from pain; no rib fracture. Possible L base consolidation (consider PE); CTA chest if concern. Low lung volumes likely explain apparent cardiomediastinal enlargement.
Chronic mild-moderate biatrial cardiomegaly. Lungs clear; no pulmonary vascular abnormality, edema, effusion, pneumonia, or CHF. Moderate thoracic scoliosis. RA/RV pacer leads in place.
Chest tubes removed. No definite pneumothorax. Low volumes. Bibasilar opacities likely effusion/atelectasis; possible pneumonia/aspiration. Residual left lower chest/upper abdomen subcutaneous gas.
Compared to prior: lung hyperexpansion with diffuse interstitial markings c/w ILD. Bilateral apical pleural thickening. Mildly increased left base opacity; ILD/atelectasis vs superimposed pneumonia.

XR can't assess sternal erosions/malignancy/costochondritis; CT advised but may not diagnose it. Progressed: LL interstitial changes; UL consolidation/bronchiectasis. NSIP vs pulmonary fibroelastosis.
Hyperinflation suggests emphysema. Hx severe tracheobronchomalacia. Stable RUL mediastinal-adjacent scar with probable bronchiectasis. Lungs otherwise clear. Heart normal size. No pleural effusion.
Improved inspiration vs prior. Post-CABG with midline sternal wires and dual-chamber pacer (RA and RV apex leads). No pneumonia, vascular congestion, or pneumothorax. Minimal left basal atelectasis.
Right PICC tip in the right atrium; to position in the lower SVC, retract the catheter 4 cm.
Interval increase in interstitial changes; favored ILD progression vs congestion/atypical infection. New/increased retrocardiac opacity: atelectasis/fibrosis vs infection. Clinical correlation.
Lateral radiograph: retrocardiac anterior left lower lobe peribronchial opacity with air bronchograms, consistent with LLL pneumonia. Heart size normal. No pleural effusion. Port-A-Cath unchanged.
Stable post-op chest s/p sternotomy and AVR. Bibasilar opacities likely atelectasis/scarring. Decreasing bilateral pleural effusions. No edema/pneumothorax. Hyperinflated lungs suggest emphysema.
Stable exam: right pigtail unchanged; no right pneumothorax; right lung expanded; hyperlucent lateral stripes are skin folds; stable right apical fiducial/opacity; left lung/heart normal.
Large right pleural effusion, redistributed, unchanged vs prior. Normal heart size. Left posterior mediastinal bulge likely from effusion. RLL atelectasis. RUL and left lung clear. No pneumothorax.
Rotated exam. Cardiomegaly and tortuous aorta unchanged; no pulmonary edema. Worsened LLL opacity and new patchy/linear right basilar opacities—atelectasis vs aspiration; ? aspiration pneumonia.
Vs prior: right lung ventilation improved; minimal right pleural effusion resolved. Left large postoperative parenchymal opacity unchanged. No new opacities/pneumonia. Cardiac silhouette normal.
Left basal masslike lesion concerning for infection. RLL opacity may be atelectasis vs less likely pneumonia. New small pleural effusions. Heart normal; upper lungs clear. Feeding tube in stomach.
Smaller mediastinum; persistent postop ant mediastinal fluid, likely resolving/redistributed. Left linear atelectasis with improved aeration; no consolidation. Less vascular engorgement; no edema.
Large left posterior pleural fluid loculation unchanged. Small left diaphragm/costal pleural thickening/fluid reduced. Chronic empyema possible; clinical eval needed. Right lung clear; heart normal.
No improvement in large left posterior loculated pleural effusion. Small pleural thickening/fluid likely decreased. Chronic empyema? No increase in pleural fluid. Right lung clear; heart normal.

Severe emphysema and severe biapical scarring. RUL nodule resection clips. CT suggests possible increased R hilar nodes. No pneumonia, decompensated chronic mild cardiomegaly, atelectasis, or effusion.
Cardiomegaly; tortuous descending aorta. Intact sternal sutures. No focal pneumonia, vascular congestion, or pleural effusion. Right paratracheal prominence likely brachiocephalic dilation.
Compared to prior, persistent low lung volumes. Heart size normal. Interstitial lung disease improved, suggesting less vascular congestion. Bilateral costophrenic blunting and basal atelectasis.
Low lung volumes; chronic mod cardiomegaly. Stable L mid-lung interstitial change; ?ILD. R tracheobronchial fullness: azygos dilation(portal HTN)/adenopathy. No PNA. CT if liver transplant planned.
Right IJ sheath removed. Postop mediastinal widening and cardiomegaly. Retrocardiac opacity less; pleural fluid and LLL volume loss. Minimal pneumopericardium/mediastinum persists. Right lung clear.
R IJ sheath out. Postop mediastinal widening/cardiomegaly. Retrocardiac opacity slightly less, c/w pleural effusion and LLL volume loss. Minimal pneumopericardium/mediastinum persist. R lung clear.

Stable heart and mediastinum. Possible new 7x11 mm nodular opacity above left hilum (LUL). Lungs otherwise clear. No effusion/pneumothorax. Linear LLL atelectasis. Recommend chest CT before treatment.
Heart and mediastinum stable. Possible new 7×11 mm nodular LUL opacity near left hilum. Lungs otherwise clear. No effusion/pneumothorax. Linear LLL atelectasis. Recommend chest CT before treatment.
New right heart border obscuration may reflect atelectasis; aspiration/pneumonia not excluded. Moderate left pleural effusion decreased with overlying atelectasis. Results relayed at 3:52 a.m.
Markedly increased left chest wall SQ emphysema to neck. Small medial left PTX; gas in effusion. Possible bronchocutaneous tract at chest tube. Increased bibasilar atelectasis. Heart size normal.
Compared to preop CXR: sternotomy and aortic valve replacement; heart size stable; no lung congestion; unchanged apical extrapericardial fat pad and left basal linear scarring; no acute lung disease.
Small L pleural effusion and elevated L hemidiaphragm unchanged from prior; smaller than before. Normal heart/mediastinum; no pneumothorax. LUL nodule unchanged; benign granuloma/hamartoma.
Sharp left fissure: small–moderate left pleural effusion (increased vs prior) vs LLL consol.; obliques to distinguish. Mod cardiomegaly, severe vascular congestion, chronic mild interstitial change.
Thoracic scoliosis with rib asymmetry persists. Chronic right pleural effusion decreased but present; better seen on lateral. Moderate cardiomegaly. No pulmonary edema or pneumothorax.
Vs prior, monitoring/support devices removed. L pectoral pacemaker/leads and sternal wires unchanged. Mod cardiomegaly. Mild-mod bilat effusions. Retrocardiac atelectasis. No pulm edema/PNA.
Vs prior CXR: asymmetric edema nearly resolved. Mod Lt pleural eff sl ↓; lingular/LLL atelectasis sl improved; tiny Lt PTX improved. Rt small eff and RLL opacity worse (atelectasis/aspiration/PNA).
Loculated R upper hemothorax/hydropneumothorax increased (craniocaudal ~7.5 cm). R basal pleural effusion. R lung partially expanded. Left lower lobe improved; minimal left fluid and linear scarring.

Vs prior: mild increase of L apical cavitary lesion with focal parenchymal reaction. L hemithorax ↓ from lingular fibrosis. RUL ?calcified nodule evident. No cardiomegaly/pleural effusions. Repeat CT.
Small pleural effusions and basilar atelectasis slightly improved. No new consolidation/pneumonia. Prominent hila (vascularity vs lymphadenopathy) in HCC. Consider contrast-enhanced chest CT.
Persistent R hemidiaphragm elevation with increased R basilar atelectasis. L mid-lung nodules slightly smaller vs prior but larger than earlier film; may reflect hemorrhage or improving infection.
Right lower lobe pneumonia with posterior/right basal opacities; left basal atelectasis. No vascular congestion.
L chest tube; small stable L apical PTX. Emphysema. Small L effusion. sl ↑ L chest wall SQ emphysema. Bilat XRT changes stable. No edema. CM unchanged. Marked T kyphosis; mid-T comp fx stable.
Little change; no acute cardiopulmonary disease. Mild hyperinflation/flattened diaphragms c/w chronic lung disease. No pneumonia/vascular congestion/effusion or ILD to suggest amiodarone toxicity.
Left lower lobe heterogeneous opacities with blunted left costophrenic angle, likely from infection, atelectasis, and/or effusion. Findings communicated at 2:33 a.m., ~2 min after discovery.
Moderate, increased cardiomegaly; consider pericardial effusion vs true enlargement. Mild-moderate pulm edema. Focal infrahilar opacity (edema vs pneumonia/atelectasis). Short-term CXR f/u Clin corr.
No interval change. Lateral view: small posterior Bochdalek hernia. Normal lung volumes. Mild bilateral apical scarring. Borderline heart size, no edema. Severe scoliosis with rib asymmetry.
Right transjugular port unchanged at cavoatrial junction vs prior. No mediastinal widening/paratracheal thickening. Cardiomediastinal normal. Low lung volumes; lungs clear. No pleural abnormality.
Elevated left hemidiaphragm. Stable postsurgical changes L hemithorax. Patchy medial R base opacities-atelectasis vs pneumonia; correlate. No PTX/pulm edema or large effusions. Low volumes. s/p LUL
2.2 cm rounded opacity over lower lobes near descending thoracic aorta on lateral; absent on frontal, may be summation. Nonurgent chest CT advised. No other acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
Prior right infrahilar abnormality resolved. No pneumonia or effusion. Chronic thoracic aortic dissection/aneurysm stable. Mild–moderate cardiomegaly stable. Apical pleural fat thickening unchanged.
Small nodular opacity R mid lung—nodule vs infection; recommend shallow oblique views after removing hardware. Multiple upper abdominal air-fluid levels; CT abdomen planned.
Moderate cardiomegaly with mild mediastinal venous distension. Possible tiny bilateral pleural effusions. No pulmonary edema; lungs clear. Suspected pericardial effusion; correlate with EKG/US.
Moderate cardiomegaly; clear lungs; no vascular congestion/edema. Mild mediastinal venous distension. Tiny possible bilateral pleural effusions. Pericardial effusion suspected—advise clinical/EKG/US.
Small unchanged bilat pleural effusions; lungs clear; heart normal. R jug cath at SVC origin; L PICC tip mid-low SVC. No pneumothorax/mediastinal widening. Small post-sternotomy retrosternal fluid.
Diffuse interstitial markings R>L, no effusion. Right base confluent opacities suggest focal pneumonia. If febrile, may be interstitial pneumonia. Broad ddx; clinical correlation and f/u advised.
Heart top-normal, stable; mediastinum stable; preserved lung volumes. Mild interstitial changes—possible ILD; chest CT advised. No consolidation, effusion, or PTX. Possible mild vascular congestion.
Residual right hilar/paratracheal adenopathy, decreasing per recent CT. Left lung clear; heart size normal. CXR is new baseline for follow-up instead of CT. Infusion port tip in mid-to-low SVC.
Normal heart size; no vascular congestion, pleural effusion, or pneumonia. Small nodule beneath left first rib, likely calcified granuloma. If concern for nodules, chest CT recommended.
Increased borderline cardiomegaly vs prior; no decompensation. Lungs clear; no pleural disease or central adenopathy. Thoracic spine multilevel disc narrowing and osteophytes; upper lumbar normal.
